title.narrative: SPVO – Harnessing Avocado Resources for Value Enhancement and Sustainability Transformation (HARVEST)

description.narrative: The HARVEST project aims to address social and interlinked environmental challenges in Rwanda’s avocado value chain, improving the livelihoods of smallholder farmers while promoting sustainable practices in the sector. Currently, Rwandan smallholders who cultivate avocado face issues such as low productivity, premature harvesting, post-harvest losses and limited access to high-value markets, which prevent them from earning a living income. With higher sources of revenue, farmers would be able to cover their basic needs, whilst also investing in their farms for long-term growth. The project is designed to benefit smallholder farmers, factory workers processing avocado oil and wider farming communities. An anticipated 5,000 smallholder farmers will benefit from the establishment of four avocado impact hubs that will function as decentralized centers for training, aggregation and distribution services. These hubs will facilitate access to direct and ongoing training on planting avocado seedlings, fertilizer application and harvesting avocados, as well as improved seedlings and Black Soldier Fly organic fertiliser created from avocado waste. This will enhance productivity and incomes, while the closer proximity to aggregation services will reduce costs and post-harvest losses for smallholder farmers. Furthermore, the project will explore the feasibility of getting selected groups of farmers – targeting 200 smallholders – Rainforest Alliance certified, subsequently earning premiums for their produce. Finally, employees from the avocado oil processing factory in Kigali will benefit from improved working conditions. The envisioned impact of the project is to increase smallholder farmer incomes by at least 20%, reduce post-harvest losses by 40%, and improve not just the agricultural productivity of smallholders but also enhance their soil health by the distribution of organic fertiliser. Ultimately, the project aims to create a more inclusive, resilient and sustainable avocado value chain, by addressing key social sustainability risks such as limited incomes and livelihoods and factory working conditions.
